text:
sara_support: FYI customer_james (acct 8241) reporting a big spike in 5xxs hitting hosted inference since ~06:30 UTC. They see lots of gateway errors (502/504) and some TLS handshake timeouts in their client logs. Caller example attached: 

customer_james: running a simple curl to the API returns intermittent 502s: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"model":"gpt-x-large","input":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (18.204.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

sara_support: customer says it started shortly after a cert rotation window but the timings are fuzzy. They see a bunch of upstream errors in the dashboard: `upstream TLS handshake timeout` and `dns lookup timeout` variants together. Opening thread to triage. :eyes:

ivan_netops: thanks, i'll pull edge proxy logs and dns metrics. can you share the exact route+model and sample request ids?

customer_james: route = /v1/generate, model = gpt-x-large, example request id = req_20260315_0067 (I can provide more if needed). We saw ~18% errors in a 10m window.

julia_oncall: pasting a filtered snippet from edge-proxy logs (06:28-06:40 UTC): 
```
[06:29:12] proxy: upstream dial tcp: lookup model-internal.cluster.local on 10.10.0.2:53: read udp 10.10.5.7:54823->10.10.0.2:53: i/o timeout
[06:29:13] proxy: upstream TLS handshake timeout for backend model-backend-3
[06:29:14] proxy: 502 Bad Gateway returned to client id=req_20260315_0067
[06:35:02] proxy: got SERVFAIL from resolver for model-internal.cluster.local
```

julia_oncall: resolver IP is our egress coredns at 10.10.0.2. dns-bot also triggered an alert for outbound DNS error rate spike.

dns-bot: ALERT: outbound-dns-error-rate > 1.2% (5m) across prod-edge; top symptom: UDP timeouts -> TCP fallbacks. Context: route /v1/generate, region us-east-1.

mike_engineer: ran dig from an affected proxy node against the primary resolver: 
```
dig @10.10.0.2 model-internal.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=1
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

mike_engineer: then tried a public resolver and got a response: 
```
dig @1.1.1.1 model-internal.cluster.local +short
10.11.4.22
```

ivan_netops: this looks like our egress resolver cluster (10.10.0.2) was intermittently dropping UDP responses — maybe overloaded or hitting conntrack/ephemeral port exhaustion after the cert rotation created brief reconnections? Let's check conntrack, coredns pods, and egress NAT gateway metrics.

julia_oncall: i see elevated CPU on coredns-1 around 06:28 and a burst of UDP RECV errors in the kernel logs on a subset of proxy hosts. kernel: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" on host proxy-23.

mike_engineer: repro steps i used: 
1) ssh proxy-23 
2) tail -n 200 /var/log/kern.log | grep conntrack 
3) dig @10.10.0.2 model-internal.cluster.local 

mike_engineer: also ran a quick traceroute to resolver: 
```
traceroute 10.10.0.2
 1  10.10.5.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  10.10.0.2  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
```

ivan_netops: ok this is consistent with conntrack exhaustion on the proxy pool — lots of short-lived DNS UDP flows during the cert rotation (proxies re-establishing outbound TLS sessions) caused the conntrack table to fill -> kernel dropped UDP replies -> coredns appears to time out -> proxy surfaces upstream TLS handshake timeouts -> 5xx to client.

sara_support: what's the customer impact window and remediation options we can offer right now?

ivan_netops: immediate mitigations: (1) add a TCP-based fallback for DNS queries on the proxy (longer latency but reliable), (2) add secondary public resolvers (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) to egress config, (3) increase conntrack table size on proxy hosts, (4) throttle reconnection bursts during rotation next time. we'll do (2) and (3) now to stop immediate drops.

mike_engineer: rolling a small change now: update proxy resolver list to [10.10.0.2, 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8] and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on the most affected pool. will patch via deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: rolling change deploy started: proxy-config/egress-resolver v3 -> v4 to pool=proxy-prod-1 (2 hosts)

julia_oncall: flushed coredns cache on coredns-1 and -2 and bumped conntrack on proxy-23 and proxy-24. watching metrics.

(10 minutes later) dns-bot: RESOLVED: outbound-dns-error-rate back to baseline 0.03% (5m).

customer_james: confirming — errors dropped to near zero after ~06:45 UTC, latency normal. Thanks for the fast turnaround, appreciate the explanation.

sara_support: closing loop with the customer. We'll add a postmortem action: document conntrack sizing guidance and include resolver fallbacks during cert rotations in runbook.

ivan_netops: noted. follow-ups: 1) runbook update, 2) consider switching DNS queries to TCP for critical paths, 3) monitor conntrack high-water marks as part of deploy gating for cert rotations.

sara_support: tagged for postmortem and runbook edits. thanks all. :tada:
